title: ProjectE vendor model registry report
description: Output of tools/scripts/sim/model_registry.py. Records which vendor model every simulation rests on and whether it may be used for a given query. 'judges_accuracy' is pinned false: whether a model is RIGHT is sim/correlate.py's question and needs a measurement. This answers a different one - WHICH model, and may it be used HERE.

judges_accuracy.description: This tool never says a model is accurate. It says which model was used, that the file is the vetted one, that the query lies inside the declared characterisation range, and that the authority tier permits the claim being made.

authority.description: NO DEFAULT. Defaulting to the weakest tier silently demotes a genuine vendor file, and the demotion is invisible at the point somebody wonders why a gate will not open; defaulting to the strongest is obviously wrong. An unlabelled model does not load.

may_signoff.description: True only for vendor_published. A derived fit is ours and the vendor never validated it; a synthetic model exists to exercise the machinery.

provenance.description: 'revision' and 'accessed' are required because a vendor document without them names a FAMILY of documents, and the one that was actually read is not recoverable later.

valid_range.description: REQUIRED. Every reader in this bundle will interpolate off the end of its data without raising - skrf returns an S21 for a frequency the file never measured. The declared envelope is the only place that can refuse.

unit.description: Mandatory and never inferred. A range of 0..10 is not a range until somebody says whether that is Hz, GHz or degrees.

load_errors.description: Collected, not raised: one malformed entry must not hide the state of the other forty. Still makes the run RED - a model that does not load is a model nothing can account for.

envelope_checks.description: The declared range compared against what the file itself contains. An overclaim is a FAIL somebody can fix by correcting the entry; an unverifiable declaration is NO_COVERAGE, a limit of this tool. Merging the two is how a registry stops being evidence.

grant.description: What the clearance ESTABLISHES, kept separate from the status so a reader cannot mistake a screening clearance for a sign-off clearance.

grants.description: Clearances counted by what they GRANT. A run that cleared four screening queries and no sign-off must not read like one that cleared four sign-offs.
